Rounded to the nearest tenth, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
question.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266178/assets/2bdf5043e8bd25884eeda042c276fad2e5fa267e1f9f19d9271564576965d09a.png)

 

First we find the area for $△ABD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 10\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{110}^{∘} \\  & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{110}^{∘} \\  & ≈28.190\,7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for $△BCD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BDC} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 13\cdot 15\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{58}^{∘} \\  & =97.5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{58}^{∘} \\  & ≈82.684\,7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BDC} \\  & =28.190\,7+82.684\,7 \\  & =110.875\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest tenth, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $110.9.$
